searchDocs.title: Getting a vault​
searchDocs.content: There are two ways to retrieve a player's vault:  local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) local S = Data.Server:GetVault(Player)   LoadVault waits until the player's data is ready. It returns nil if the data cannot be loaded, such as when the player leaves or LoadTimeout expires.  Always check its return value before using the vault:  local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) if not S then return end   GetVault never waits. It returns the existing vault if the player's data is already loaded, otherwise nil. This is useful in code that runs after loading, such as remote handlers.

searchDocs.title: Non-player sessions​
searchDocs.content: You can also pass a string key instead of a Player:  local Guild = Data.Server:LoadVault("Guild_42")   This opens a session that isn't tied to a specific player. It can be useful for data shared across a guild, world, or other keyed entity.

searchDocs.title: Reading data​
searchDocs.content: Every value in the template can be accessed through its corresponding node:  local Coins = S.Coins.Get() local Level = S.Stats.Level.Get() local Stats = S.Stats.Get()   You can access nested values by chaining keys. The returned value from Get corresponds to the node you called it on.

searchDocs.title: Client-side reads​
searchDocs.content: On the client, tables returned by Get are read-only proxies by default.  You can read and traverse them normally, but attempting to modify them throws an error. This helps prevent accidental local changes from making UI state disagree with the server.  If you need the raw table instead, you can disable this behavior with ClientGuard = "Off".

searchDocs.title: Writing data​
searchDocs.content: All writes go through node methods rather than direct assignment.

searchDocs.title: Set​
searchDocs.content: Set replaces a node's current value:  S.Coins.Set(50) S.Stats.Level.Set(2)   It also supports optional fields:  S.Equipped.Set("Wooden Sword") S.Equipped.Set(nil)   Both calls are valid because Equipped is optional in the template.

searchDocs.title: Update​
searchDocs.content: Update receives the current value and returns its replacement:  S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 10 end)   This is useful when the next value depends on the previous one.  Both Set and Update return the new value.  tip No direct assignment S.Coins = 50 -- throws Data nodes aren't ordinary tables. Writes must go through their methods so Strata can track changes and replicate them correctly.

searchDocs.title: Mutating tables​
searchDocs.content: For changes involving multiple fields, use Mutate.  S.Stats.Mutate(function(Stats) Stats.Level += 1 Stats.Xp = 0 end)   Strata tracks the changes made during the mutation and replicates the resulting changes rather than requiring you to replace the entire table.

searchDocs.title: Snapshots​
searchDocs.content: Snapshot returns a deep copy of the current value.  local Before = S.Stats.Snapshot()   Unlike a read-only proxy, a snapshot can be modified freely without changing the actual vault.  This is useful when you need to keep a previous version of some data, prepare changes separately, or pass a copy to another system.

searchDocs.title: Arrays​
searchDocs.content: Strata provides methods for common array operations.  S.Inventory.Push("Wooden Sword") S.Inventory.Push("Shield")   Push adds an item to the end of the array and returns the new length.  S.Inventory.InsertAt(1, "Torch")   InsertAt inserts an item at the specified position, shifting subsequent elements.  local Removed = S.Inventory.RemoveAt(2) local Last = S.Inventory.Pop()   RemoveAt removes and returns the item at a position. Pop removes and returns the last item.  You can also use Size to retrieve the number of entries:  print(S.Inventory.Size())

searchDocs.title: Dictionaries​
searchDocs.content: Dictionaries use the same node API as other tables.  S.Items.Insert("sword_001", { Damage = 12, })   You can access individual entries directly:  local Damage = S.Items.sword_001.Damage.Get()   Use Has to check whether an entry exists:  print(S.Items.Has("sword_001"))   Remove deletes an entry and returns its previous value:  local Removed = S.Items.Remove("sword_001")

searchDocs.title: Shared collection methods​
searchDocs.content: Arrays and dictionaries also support:  Keys — Returns the collection's keys.Values — Returns its values.Size — Returns the number of entries.Clear — Removes all entries.  These methods are available on both collection types.

searchDocs.title: Observing changes​
searchDocs.content: Strata provides one Observe method on the root state. It accepts a path and returns a function that registers a listener.  local Connection = S.Observe("Stats.Level")(function(Level) print("Level is", Level) end)   The listener runs immediately with the current value, then runs again whenever that value changes.  The returned connection can be disconnected when you no longer need the observation:  Connection.Disconnect()

searchDocs.title: Choosing a path​
searchDocs.content: The path determines which part of the vault you're observing.  S.Observe("Coins")(OnCoins) S.Observe("Stats")(OnStats) S.Observe()(OnEntireData)   "Coins" observes a single field."Stats" observes the entire Stats table.An empty path observes the entire vault.  Paths can also be provided as tables.

searchDocs.title: Parent and child observations​
searchDocs.content: Observations account for changes throughout the selected path.  Observing a parent fires when one of its descendants changes.Observing a child fires when its parent is replaced.Unchanged values do not trigger another callback.  The callback value is typed according to the selected path. For example, observing "Coins" gives the listener a number, while observing "Stats" gives it the corresponding table type.  Your editor can autocomplete valid paths from the template.

searchDocs.title: Client observations​
searchDocs.content: The client uses the same root-level Observe method:  local C = Data.Client:LoadVault() if C then C.Observe("Coins")(function(Coins) CoinLabel.Text = tostring(Coins) end) end   There is no separate client observation API. Server-side changes are replicated, and client observations respond to those changes.

searchDocs.title: Sessions​
searchDocs.content: Strata manages session loading, saving, and cleanup automatically. You can still interact with a session directly when needed.  S.Save() S.End() print(S.IsLoaded())   Save requests an immediate save.End ends the session.IsLoaded checks whether the session is still active.

searchDocs.title: Session information​
searchDocs.content: Use GetSessionInfo to retrieve information about a session:  local Info = S.GetSessionInfo() print(Info.UserId) print(Info.LoadedAt) print(Info.LastSaveAt) print(Info.IsActive)

searchDocs.title: Iterating loaded sessions​
searchDocs.content: ForEachSession lets you perform an operation on every currently loaded session:  Data.Server:ForEachSession(function(Key, S, Info) S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 5 end) end)   When the server shuts down, active sessions are saved and ended automatically.

searchDocs.title: Metadata​
searchDocs.content: Each session has a metadata table alongside its data.  Metadata is stored with the profile, but it isn't part of the template. This makes it useful for bookkeeping values that don't belong in the main data structure.  S.SetMeta("LastDevice", "Mobile") print(S.GetMeta("LastDevice"))

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Server-side changes are replicated to the client automatically.  You don't need to create remotes, manually send updates, or request replication after every write.  Strata batches changes made within the same tick. This means multiple writes can be grouped into a single replication update instead of being sent individually.  The client receives a read-only replica. It can read and observe data, but all modifications must happen on the server.

searchDocs.title: Supported values​
searchDocs.content: Strata supports standard Luau values such as:  NumbersStringsBooleansOptional fieldsArraysDictionariesBuffers  It also automatically serializes supported Roblox datatypes, including Vector3, CFrame, Color3, UDim2, EnumItem, and DateTime.  These values are converted for storage and restored when loaded. You can use supported datatypes directly in your template without manually writing serialization logic.

searchDocs.title: Data limitations​
searchDocs.content: Strata follows ProfileStore's underlying data restrictions:  Arrays cannot contain gaps.Tables cannot mix numeric and string keys.Instances, functions, and threads cannot be saved.  Keep these restrictions in mind when designing your template.

searchDocs.title: What makes Strata easy?​
searchDocs.content: No session setup. Player sessions are handled automatically.No remotes to manage. Replication is built in.No separate type definitions. Your template provides types and autocomplete.No manual serialization. Supported Roblox and Luau datatypes are handled automatically.No manual saving. Data saves automatically, and you can still call Save when needed.  info For the best autocomplete experience, enable the new Luau type solver by setting Workspace.UseNewLuauTypeSolver to Enabled. Runtime functionality does not depend on it.

searchDocs.title: 1. Install Strata​
searchDocs.content: Place Strata inside ReplicatedStorage. Strata automatically creates its required runtime components.

searchDocs.title: 2. Create your data module​
searchDocs.content: Create a ModuleScript named Data inside ReplicatedStorage:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Strata = require(ReplicatedStorage.Strata) local Template = { Coins = 0, Stats = { Level = 1, Xp = 0, }, Inventory = {} :: { string }, } return Strata:Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, })   The template defines your data structure and provides the types used throughout your project.  New players receive the template, while existing player data is reconciled with newly added fields.

searchDocs.title: 3. Load and use data​
searchDocs.content: Server  local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data) Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(Player) local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) if not S then return end S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 100 end) S.Inventory.Push("Wooden Sword") end)   Client  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data) local C = Data.Client:LoadVault() if C then C.Observe("Coins")(function(Coins) CoinLabel.Text = tostring(Coins) end) end   Observe takes a path from the root state and returns a function that accepts your listener. It immediately provides the current value, then runs again whenever that value changes.

searchDocs.title: Working with data​
searchDocs.content: Strata provides methods based on the type of value you're working with.

searchDocs.title: Any value​
searchDocs.content: Get — Retrieve the current value.Set — Replace the current value.Update — Transform the current value.

searchDocs.title: Tables​
searchDocs.content: Mutate — Modify a table.Snapshot — Retrieve a copy of the current data.

searchDocs.title: Arrays​
searchDocs.content: Push — Add an item to the end.Pop — Remove the last item.InsertAt — Insert an item at a position.RemoveAt — Remove an item at a position.

searchDocs.title: Arrays and maps​
searchDocs.content: Has — Check whether a key or value exists.Keys — Retrieve keys.Values — Retrieve values.Size — Get the number of entries.Insert — Insert an entry.Remove — Remove an entry.Clear — Remove all entries.

searchDocs.title: Vault operations​
searchDocs.content: Observe — Subscribe to changes at a path.Save — Save the current data.End — End a session.Replicate — Request replication.GetSessionInfo — Retrieve session information.IsLoaded — Check whether a vault is loaded.  All data-node methods use dot syntax:  S.Coins.Get() S.Coins.Set(100) S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 1 end)   Observe is the exception in terms of where it lives: it is exposed once on the root state and takes a path.  S.Observe("Stats.Level")(function(Level) print("Level:", Level) end)

searchDocs.title: Batched replication​
searchDocs.content: Strata groups server-side changes together before replicating them. Multiple changes made within the same tick can be sent as a single update rather than separate network updates.

searchDocs.title: What Strata is for​
searchDocs.content: Strata is designed for player data.  It uses ProfileStore for session-based data saving and provides automatic client replication. It is not intended to replace systems such as OrderedDataStore or MessagingService for global data, leaderboards, or communication between servers.  The server owns all data changes. The client receives a read-only replica, and server-side changes are replicated automatically.

searchDocs.title: Open​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.Open(Options: Config<T>) → StrataClient<T> Opens or retrieves a client replica for a Strata store. Creates a client replica if one does not already exist. Subsequent calls for the same store reuse the existing replica. The returned client automatically requests its initial data and receives subsequent replication updates.

searchDocs.title: LoadVault​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.LoadVault(self: StrataClient<T>) → State<T>? Waits for the initial replica to become available. Returns the State instance once the replica has loaded. Returns nil if the configured loading timeout is reached.

searchDocs.title: GetVault​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.GetVault(self: StrataClient<T>) → State<T>? Retrieves the existing client replica without waiting. Returns nil if the replica has not loaded yet.

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.IsLoaded(self: StrataClient<T>) → boolean Checks whether the client replica has loaded.

searchDocs.title: GetSettings​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.GetSettings(self: StrataClient<T>) → CachedSettings Retrieves the cached configuration for this client store.

searchDocs.title: RequestSyncAPI​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataClient.RequestSyncAPI(self: StrataClient<T>) → () Requests a full synchronization of the client replica from the server.

searchDocs.title: Open​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.Open(Options: Config<T>) → StrataServer<T> Initializes a server store and its session manager. Creates the underlying ProfileStore and automatically manages player sessions, saving, replication, and cleanup.

searchDocs.title: LoadVault​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.LoadVault( self: StrataServer<T>, Target: Player | string ) → State<T>? Loads or retrieves a player's data vault. Waits for the session to become available before returning its State interface. Returns nil if the session cannot be loaded or the loading timeout is reached. Accepts either a Player or a string session key.

searchDocs.title: GetVault​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.GetVault( self: StrataServer<T>, Target: Player | string ) → State<T>? Retrieves an existing data vault without waiting. Returns nil if the session has not loaded or is no longer active. Accepts either a Player or a string session key.

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.IsLoaded( self: StrataServer<T>, Target: Player | string ) → boolean Checks whether a session is currently loaded and active. Accepts either a Player or a string session key.

searchDocs.title: GetSessionInfoAPI​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.GetSessionInfoAPI( self: StrataServer<T>, Target: Player | string ) → SessionInfo? Retrieves information about an active session. Returns nil if the session is not active. Accepts either a Player or a string session key.

searchDocs.title: GetSettings​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.GetSettings(self: StrataServer<T>) → CachedSettings Retrieves the cached configuration for this store.

searchDocs.title: GetPlayerFromKey​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.GetPlayerFromKey( self: StrataServer<T>, Key: string ) → Player?  Retrieves the Player associated with a session key. Returns nil if the session is not associated with a player.

searchDocs.title: ForEachSession​
searchDocs.content: </> StrataServer.ForEachSession( self: StrataServer<T>, Callback: ( Key: string, State: State<T>, Info: SessionInfo ) → () ) → () Iterates over all currently active sessions. Provides each session's key, State interface, and session information to the callback.

searchDocs.title: Version​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Strata.Version: string

searchDocs.title: Init​
searchDocs.content: </> Strata:Init(Options: Config<T>) → { Server: StrataServer<T>, Client: StrataClient<T> } Opens a Strata for the current environment.Server is only populated on the server, Client only on the client. The other side is nil at runtime, so each side can use its own field without nil checks.

searchDocs.title: Bridge​
searchDocs.content: </> type Bridge = {} Defines the communication interface between a State node and its underlying session. Provides access to session data, mutation operations, observation, replication, and session metadata. GetRoot: (Key: string) -> any?, IsLoaded: (Key: string) -> boolean, Write: ((Key: string, Path: { any }, Value: any) -> ())?, Mutate: ((Key: string, Path: { any }, Mutator: (Target: any) -> (), Full: boolean?) -> ())?, Observe: (Key: string, TagPath: { any }?, Listener: (Value: any) -> ()) -> { Disconnect: (...any) -> () }, Save: ((Key: string) -> ())?, End: ((Key: string) -> ())?, Replicate: ((Key: string, Target: Player?) -> ())?, GetSessionInfo: ((Key: string) -> any?)?, GetMeta: ((Key: string, MetaKey: string?) -> any)?, SetMeta: ((Key: string, MetaKey: string, Value: any) -> ())?, ReadOnly: boolean, Guard: boolean, }

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> State.new( Bridge: Bridge,-- Backend interface used by the state. Key: string-- Session key associated with the state. ) → Node Creates a new state node for a session. The returned node represents the root of the session's data. Child nodes are created automatically when accessing nested properties.

searchDocs.title: JSONAcceptable​
searchDocs.content: </> type JSONAcceptable = {JSONAcceptable} | {[string]: JSONAcceptable} | number | string | boolean | buffer Values that can be serialized by Strata's underlying data system. Supports recursive tables, primitive values, and buffers.

searchDocs.title: Path​
searchDocs.content: </> type Path = {any} Represents a path used to access a nested value in a State.

searchDocs.title: Connection​
searchDocs.content: </> type Connection = {Disconnect: (...any) → ()} Represents a disconnectable subscription. Provides a Disconnect method to stop receiving notifications.

searchDocs.title: MutateContext​
searchDocs.content: </> type MutateContext = { Key: string, Player: Player? , Data: T, Path: Path? } Context provided to mutation lifecycle callbacks. Contains the session key, associated player, current data, and optional path affected by the mutation.

searchDocs.title: ReplicateMode​
searchDocs.content: </> type ReplicateMode = "Diff" | "Full" | "Hybrid" Controls how Strata replicates data to clients. Diff: Replicates changes as patches. Full: Replicates the complete state. Hybrid: Uses patches with full-state replication when appropriate.

searchDocs.title: ClientGuard​
searchDocs.content: </> type ClientGuard = "Proxy" | "Off" Controls how the client handles access to replicated data. Proxy: Uses guarded access. Off: Disables the client guard.

searchDocs.title: SessionInfo​
searchDocs.content: </> type SessionInfo = { Key: string, Player: Player? , UserId: number?, LoadedAt: number, LastSaveAt: number?, Seq: number, IsActive: boolean } Describes the current state and metadata of a loaded session.

searchDocs.title: CachedSettings​
searchDocs.content: </> type CachedSettings = table A snapshot of the effective settings used by a Strata store. Contains the resolved configuration, including defaults for omitted options.

searchDocs.title: State<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type State<T> = Session<T> Represents the complete typed state interface for a Strata store. Provides root-level access to data, nested nodes, collection operations, session methods, and observation. Requires the new Luau type solver for accurate type inference.

searchDocs.title: Node<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type Node<T> = Access<T> Represents a typed node within a Strata state. Provides type-aware access to values and nested tables, with methods appropriate to the underlying value type. Requires the new Luau type solver for accurate type inference.

searchDocs.title: StrataServer<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type StrataServer<T> = {} Server interface for a Strata store. Provides methods for loading and accessing player sessions, checking session status, retrieving session information, and iterating over active sessions. LoadVault: (self: StrataServer<T>, Target: string | Player) -> State<T>?, GetVault: (self: StrataServer<T>, Target: string | Player) -> State<T>?, IsLoaded: (self: StrataServer<T>, Target: string | Player) -> boolean, GetSessionInfo: (self: StrataServer<T>, Target: string | Player) -> SessionInfo?, GetSettings: (self: StrataServer<T>) -> CachedSettings, GetPlayerFromKey: (self: StrataServer<T>, Key: string) -> Player?, ForEachSession: (self: StrataServer<T>, Callback: (Key: string, State: State<T>, Info: SessionInfo) -> ()) -> (), }

searchDocs.title: StrataClient<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type StrataClient<T> = {} Client interface for a Strata store. Provides access to the client's replicated state, loading status, store settings, and manual synchronization. The client replica is read-only. LoadVault: (self: StrataClient<T>) -> State<T>?, GetVault: (self: StrataClient<T>) -> State<T>?, IsLoaded: (self: StrataClient<T>) -> boolean, GetSettings: (self: StrataClient<T>) -> CachedSettings, RequestSync: (self: StrataClient<T>) -> (), }

searchDocs.title: Config<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type Config<T> = {} Configuration used to initialize a Strata store. StoreName and Template are required. All other properties are optional and use Strata's defaults when omitted. Includes session lifecycle hooks, mutation callbacks, replication settings, and data migration options. StoreName: string, Template: T, Leaderstats: Flags<T>?, KeyPrefix: string?, PlayerKey: ((Player) -> string)?, Mock: boolean?, KickOnFail: boolean?, KickOnSessionEnd: boolean?, KickMessage: string?, LoadTimeout: number?, SchemaVersion: number?, Migrate: ((Data: T, FromVersion: number, ToVersion: number) -> ())?, AutoSaveSeconds: number?, ReplicateMode: ReplicateMode?, MaxPatchesBeforeFull: number?, CollapsePatchesAt: number?, FlushImmediately: boolean?, ReplicateOnSave: boolean?, ClientGuard: ClientGuard?, BeforeMutate: ((Context: MutateContext<T>) -> ())?, AfterMutate: ((Context: MutateContext<T>) -> ())?, OnSessionStart: ((Key: string, Player: Player?, Data: T) -> ())?, OnSessionEnd: ((Key: string, Player: Player?) -> ())?, }

searchDocs.title: Profile<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type Profile<T> = {} Describes the ProfileStore session interface used internally by Strata. Contains the underlying data, metadata, user IDs, and session lifecycle and saving methods. Data: T, RobloxMetaData: JSONAcceptable, UserIds: { number }, Key: string, OnSessionEnd: any, IsActive: (self: Profile<T>) -> boolean, Reconcile: (self: Profile<T>) -> (), EndSession: (self: Profile<T>) -> (), AddUserId: (self: Profile<T>, UserId: number) -> (), Save: (self: Profile<T>) -> (), }

searchDocs.title: ReplicaPath​
searchDocs.content: </> type ReplicaPath = { Path: Path, Value: any } Represents an individual data replication patch. Contains the path being modified and the value associated with that path.

searchDocs.title: Storage​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesStoreName	none	The DataStore name. Change it to start a fresh, separate store. Template	none	The shape and default values of a player's data. KeyPrefix	""	Prepended to the player's UserId to build their save key. PlayerKey	KeyPrefix .. UserId	A function (Player) -> string for full control over save keys. Mock	false	Uses ProfileStore's in-memory storage. Nothing is saved. Good for tests. AutoSaveSeconds	unset	Adds a save every N seconds on top of ProfileStore's own auto-saving.

searchDocs.title: Sessions​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesLoadTimeout	30	Seconds LoadVault waits before giving up and returning nil. KickOnFail	true	Kick a player whose data couldn't load, so they never play on empty data. KickOnSessionEnd	true	Kick a player if their session ends while they're still in the server. KickMessage	"Could not load your data. Please rejoin."	The message shown when a player is kicked.  caution Leave KickOnFail on unless you have a plan for players with no data. With it off, a player whose data failed to load stays in the game with no vault, and LoadVault returns nil for them.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesReplicateMode	"Hybrid"	How changes reach the client. See below. MaxPatchesBeforeFull	24	Once this many patches queue up in a frame, send a full snapshot instead. CollapsePatchesAt	12	If one Mutate changes this many keys in a table, send the table as a single patch. FlushImmediately	false	Send each change right away instead of batching them. ReplicateOnSave	false	Send a full snapshot to the client after every manual Save.  ReplicateMode takes three values:  "Hybrid" is the default. It sends small patches and switches to a full snapshot when a frame has too many of them."Diff" sends patches."Full" always sends the whole table. It's simpler to reason about, and it costs more bandwidth on large data.  Each replica carries a sequence number. If a patch is ever missed, the client notices and asks the server for a fresh snapshot by itself.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesClientGuard	"Proxy"	"Proxy" returns read-only tables from Get on the client. "Off" returns the raw table.

searchDocs.title: Leaderstats​
searchDocs.content: Name top-level fields that should appear on the Roblox leaderboard. They must be numbers, strings or booleans.  Strata:Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, Leaderstats = { Coins = true }, })   Strata creates the leaderstats folder and keeps it in sync with the data. You never touch the values yourself.

searchDocs.title: Hooks​
searchDocs.content: Hooks let you react to data events without wrapping every call. Errors inside a hook are caught, so a bad hook never breaks a write.  Strata:Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, OnSessionStart = function(Key, Player, Data) print("Loaded", Key) end, OnSessionEnd = function(Key, Player) print("Ended", Key) end, BeforeMutate = function(Context) -- Context.Key, Context.Player, Context.Data, Context.Path end, AfterMutate = function(Context) print(Context.Key, "changed", table.concat(Context.Path or {}, ".")) end, })   Hook	Receives	RunsOnSessionStart	Key, Player?, Data	After a session loads, before the client is sent its data. OnSessionEnd	Key, Player?	Just before a session ends. BeforeMutate	Context	Before every server write. AfterMutate	Context	After every server write.

searchDocs.title: Changing your template later​
searchDocs.content: Adding a field to the template is safe. Existing players get the new field and its default the next time they load, and any field whose type changed is reset to the template's value.  For changes that need real logic, like renaming a field or converting a format, set a SchemaVersion and write a Migrate function. It runs once per profile, when that profile's saved version is older than yours.  Strata:Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, SchemaVersion = 2, Migrate = function(Data, FromVersion, ToVersion) if FromVersion < 2 then Data.Stats.Xp = Data.Xp or 0 Data.Xp = nil end end, })   tip Bump SchemaVersion by one each time you ship a migration. Migrate always receives the profile's old version, so you can handle players who skipped several updates in a single function.

searchDocs.title: Reading settings back​
searchDocs.content: local Settings = Data.Server:GetSettings() print(Settings.ReplicateMode, Settings.LoadTimeout)   The client has the same method, so shared code can check what it's running under.
